name: glsl-lsp
description: GLSL completion, go to definition, rename and hover docs that follow your #includes, plus diagnostics, a formatter and live sliders and color pickers. For OpenGL, Vulkan, WebGL, LYGIA and Shadertoy.
author: Pablo de Groot

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, glslangValidator only runs from a path set in your user settings; a workspace cannot choose the program.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Language features need files on disk: in virtual workspaces only syntax highlighting works.

glslLsp.includePaths.markdownDescription: Extra directories searched by `#include` after the including file's folder. Relative entries are resolved against each workspace folder.

glslLsp.diagnostics.enable.description: Report problems (syntax, unresolved includes, undeclared identifiers, glslangValidator errors).

glslLsp.diagnostics.undeclared.markdownDescription: Report identifiers that resolve to nothing. Names declared in a not-yet-included workspace file are errors with an "Add #include" quick fix.

glslLsp.diagnostics.glslang.enable.markdownDescription: Validate shaders with `glslangValidator` and report its errors.

glslLsp.diagnostics.glslang.path.markdownDescription: The `glslangValidator` executable: a name looked up on `PATH` (never in the workspace folder), an absolute path, or a path relative to the first workspace folder. A `.cmd`/`.bat` wrapper works on Windows. In Restricted Mode only the value from your user settings is used.

enumDescriptions: OpenGL rules, or Vulkan 1.2 when the shader uses Vulkan-only GLSL (`layout(set = ...)`, `push_constant`, `subpassInput`, separate `texture2D`/`sampler`, `gl_VertexIndex`, ray tracing and mesh stages, Vulkan extensions).
Always OpenGL / OpenGL ES rules.
Vulkan 1.0 rules.
Vulkan 1.1 rules.
Vulkan 1.2 rules.
Vulkan 1.3 rules.
glslLsp.diagnostics.glslang.targetEnv.markdownDescription: Which rules `glslangValidator` checks with (its `--target-env`). `auto` detects Vulkan GLSL per shader.

glslLsp.diagnostics.onType.description: Re-validate while typing (debounced). When off, files are checked when opened and saved.

glslLsp.completion.autoInclude.markdownDescription: When completing a function, struct or macro from a file that is not yet included, insert the matching `#include "..."` line automatically.

glslLsp.rename.readOnlyPaths.markdownDescription: Folders whose files a rename never edits (third-party libraries such as LYGIA). Renaming a symbol declared there is refused. A bare name matches that folder anywhere; an entry containing `/` matches a path relative to the workspace folder. Files outside the workspace folders are read-only unless they are open in an editor.

enumDescriptions: No parameter name hints.
Hints only for literal arguments (numbers, booleans, constructors).
Hints for every argument whose text does not already say the parameter name.
glslLsp.inlayHints.parameterNames.markdownDescription: Parameter name inlay hints on call arguments, e.g. `smoothstep(edge0: 0.2, edge1: 0.8, x)`.

enumDescriptions: Only vec3/vec4 literals that look like colors (assigned to col, color, tint, ... or passed to such a parameter).
Every vec3/vec4 literal with components in [0, 1].
No color decorators.
glslLsp.colors.mode.markdownDescription: Which `vec3(...)` / `vec4(...)` literals get a color swatch and picker.

enumDescriptions: Per file: files that define `mainImage` or use a shader-toy directive (and the files they include or are included by) get Shadertoy support. Every file does when the shader-toy extension is installed.
Every GLSL file gets Shadertoy support.
Plain GLSL only. `mainImage` files are validated as ordinary GLSL (no generated `main`).
glslLsp.shadertoy.enable.markdownDescription: Where Shadertoy support applies: the Shadertoy uniforms (`iTime`, `iResolution`, ...) and entry points, the [shader-toy extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=stevensona.shader-toy) directives (`#iChannel`, `#iUniform`, `#iKeyboard`) and validating `mainImage` shaders inside a generated `main()`. The shader-toy extension itself is optional. The legacy values `true` and `false` still work and mean `on` and `off`.

type.markdownDescription: Builtin GLSL type (`float`, `vec3`, `mat4`, `sampler2D`, ...). Arrays are written `type[size]`, e.g. `vec4[16]`. Entries with an unknown type are ignored.

doc.markdownDescription: Markdown shown on hover and in completion.

glslLsp.environment.uniforms.markdownDescription: Uniforms your shader runtime provides beyond GLSL (and Shadertoy). They behave like builtins: hover, completion, highlighting, member and index typing, no undeclared-identifier report, and they are declared for `glslangValidator`. A file that declares the same name itself wins. Example: `[{ "name": "iCursorTrail", "type": "vec2[8]", "doc": "Last 8 cursor positions in pixels." }]`.

glslLsp.environment.defines.markdownDescription: Macros your shader runtime defines, as `{ "NAME": "value" }` (the value may be `""`). They are known to hover, completion and the undeclared-identifier check, and are passed to `glslangValidator` as `#define NAME value`. Example: `{ "MY_RUNTIME": "", "MAX_LIGHTS": "8" }`.

enumDescriptions: The uniforms and attributes three.js adds to a `ShaderMaterial` (`projectionMatrix`, `modelViewMatrix`, `position`, `uv`, ...), and `#include <chunk>` lines are not reported.

glslLsp.environment.presets.markdownDescription: Names a framework injects into your shaders, added to `#glslLsp.environment.uniforms#`. `three.js`: the `ShaderMaterial` uniforms and attributes (`modelMatrix`, `modelViewMatrix`, `projectionMatrix`, `viewMatrix`, `normalMatrix`, `cameraPosition`, `isOrthographic`, `position`, `normal`, `uv`); its `#include <chunk>` lines are not reported as unresolved.

glslLsp.index.exclude.markdownDescription: Folders skipped when indexing. A bare name (`node_modules`) matches that folder anywhere; an entry containing `/` (`vendor/old`) matches a path relative to the workspace folder, or the end of one. A folder containing a `.glsl-lsp-ignore` file is always skipped. Files in skipped folders are still loaded when something includes them.

glslLsp.index.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of GLSL files indexed per workspace.

glslLsp.values.throttleMs.markdownDescription: Minimum time in milliseconds between document edits while dragging a widget in the **Values** panel (33 ms is about 30 updates per second). Raise it if the live preview stutters.

glslLsp.values.maxDecimals.markdownDescription: Maximum number of decimals the **Values** panel writes into a float literal. Trailing zeros are always trimmed (`0.5`, `2.0`). A literal that already has more decimals keeps its precision, and a value too small for the limit is written with an exponent (`1e-5`) instead of `0.0`.

glslLsp.values.followCursor.markdownDescription: Update the **Values** panel cursor row as the editor cursor moves. When off, it updates when you switch editors or run `GLSL: Focus Values Panel`.

enumDescriptions: Only indentation, trailing whitespace, blank-line runs, the final newline, a space after `,` and `;` and around assignments. Other spacing (hand-aligned columns, aligned comments) is never changed.

Everything conservative does, plus spaces around binary operators and after `if`/`for`/`while`/`switch`/`return`, no space before a call's `(` or inside parentheses and brackets, one space before `{`, and brace placement per `glslLsp.format.braceStyle`.
No formatting: format requests return no edits.
glslLsp.format.mode.markdownDescription: How much **Format Document** / **Format Selection** / format on type change. Preprocessor lines, comments, `// glsl-format off` ... `// glsl-format on` regions and macro continuation lines are never reformatted. Lines are never wrapped.

glslLsp.format.maxBlankLines.markdownDescription: Longest run of consecutive blank lines the formatter keeps.

enumDescriptions: Leave braces where they are.
`void f() {` and `} else {`.
`{` on its own line, and `else` on the line after `}`.
glslLsp.format.braceStyle.markdownDescription: Where the `{` of a block goes. Only used when `glslLsp.format.mode` is `opinionated`; one-line blocks and initializer lists never move.

glslLsp.format.indentPreprocessor.markdownDescription: Indent preprocessor lines (`#ifdef`, `#define`, ...) to the brace depth of the surrounding code. Off: they keep their indentation.

glslLsp.trace.server.description: Trace the communication between VS Code and the GLSL language server.
